API keys are stored securely on the server-side using server-side sessions. The browser never stores keys, and the cookie is `HttpOnly`, so JavaScript cannot read it. Additionally, the cookie is sent over a secure connection (`Secure` flag) and has a `SameSite=Strict` attribute to prevent cross-site requests. The API keys are also rate-limited per key to prevent brute-force attacks.

{"question": "Find out how API keys are stored and note it down under the title 'api keys'."}

API keys are stored securely on the server-side using server-side sessions. The browser never stores keys, and the cookie is `HttpOnly`, so JavaScript cannot read it. Additionally, the cookie is sent over a secure connection (`Secure` flag) and has a `SameSite=Strict` attribute to prevent cross-site requests. The API keys are also rate-limited per key to prevent brute-force attacks.
